```{r libraries}
library(knitr)
```

```{r read_tables}
csv_dir <- file.path("csv", "RUN_nov11")
figure_dir <- file.path("figures", "RUN_nov11")
.read <- function(name){
  utils::read.csv(file.path(csv_dir, paste0(name, ".csv")),
                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
results_df <- .read("results")
score_df <- .read("scores")
block_df <- .read("blocks")
scramble_df <- .read("scramble")
oracle_df <- .read("oracle_dev")
check_df <- .read("bank_checks")

best_rule_vec <- c(marginal = "embed_prior", direct = "state_adjusted")
fmt <- function(x, digits = 3){formatC(x, digits = digits, format = "f")}

# One line of a summary block, as a number.
.block <- function(key, run, split, rule){
  bool_vec <- block_df$key == key & block_df$run == run &
    block_df$split == split & block_df$rule == rule
  stopifnot(sum(bool_vec) == 1)
  as.numeric(block_df$value[bool_vec])
}

# Per-example scores of one rule in one run and split, ordered by id.
.scores <- function(run, split, rule){
  sub_df <- score_df[score_df$run == run & score_df$split == split &
                       score_df$rule == rule, ]
  sub_df[order(sub_df$id), ]
}
.mean_score <- function(run, split, rule){mean(.scores(run, split, rule)$score)}

# Mean score of one rule in one stratum.
.stratum <- function(run, split, rule, factor_name, level){
  sub_df <- .scores(run, split, rule)
  mean(sub_df$score[as.character(sub_df[[factor_name]]) == level])
}

# The paired comparison of a run's kept rule with a reference rule.
.paired <- function(run, split, reference){
  best_df <- .scores(run, split, best_rule_vec[[run]])
  reference_df <- .scores(run, split, reference)
  stopifnot(all(best_df$id == reference_df$id))
  difference_vec <- best_df$score - reference_df$score
  list(difference = mean(difference_vec),
       num_examples = length(difference_vec),
       num_improved = sum(difference_vec < 0),
       se = stats::sd(difference_vec) / sqrt(length(difference_vec)))
}

.results <- function(run){results_df[results_df$run == run, ]}
.num_status <- function(run, status){
  sum(.results(run)$status[-1] == status)
}
.best_commit <- function(run){
  run_df <- .results(run)
  run_df$commit[max(which(run_df$status == "keep"))]
}
.code <- function(text){paste0("\x60", text, "\x60")}

# One run's log as a table.
.experiment_table <- function(run){
  run_df <- .results(run)[-1, ]
  data.frame(experiment = run_df$experiment,
             commit = .code(run_df$commit),
             status = run_df$status,
             score = fmt(run_df$score, 4),
             change = fmt(run_df$delta, 4),
             description = run_df$description,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

# Every `keep` row of both logs appears in the tables below.
stopifnot(all(results_df$status %in% c("keep", "discard")))

# The scramble check, averaged by rule and state.
scramble_mean_df <- stats::aggregate(
  scramble_df[, c("change_in_se", "change_in_se_both", "se_ratio",
                  "score_direct", "score_direct_scrambled",
                  "score_direct_both", "score_marginal",
                  "score_marginal_both")],
  by = list(rule = scramble_df$rule, state = scramble_df$state), FUN = mean
)
.scramble <- function(rule, state, column){
  scramble_mean_df[[column]][scramble_mean_df$rule == rule &
                               scramble_mean_df$state == state]
}
.oracle <- function(state, column){
  mean(oracle_df[[column]][oracle_df$state == state])
}
.check <- function(factor_name, level, column){
  check_df[[column]][check_df$factor == factor_name & check_df$level == level]
}
num_dev <- nrow(.scores("direct", "dev", "null_rescaled"))
num_test <- nrow(.scores("direct", "test", "null_rescaled"))
```

# Overview {-}

This document is built from the design memo of the second loop
(`MEMO_claude.md`), the record of its bank (`BANK.md`), the logs of its two
runs, and the tables under `csv/RUN_nov11/`. Every number in its prose is
read from those tables. It follows the sections of the autoresearch
protocol's run report, for two runs at once.

**The question.** The first loop kept `donor_wls`, a rule for the log fold
change and its standard error that uses the fitted library of eSVD-DE and
nothing of its embedding $\widehat x_c^\top \widehat y_g$. Kevin asked for
a second loop restricted to rules that use the embedding, on a bank in
which cell-state differences give the low-rank term something to
contribute. The question is whether such a rule exists, how much it gains,
and what it estimates.

The document argues five things.

1. Whether the embedding can help depends on the target. If the target is
   the log ratio of mean expression between the arms, cell-state
   differences included (the *marginal* effect), the embedding cannot
   improve the log fold change; if the target is the effect at fixed cell
   state (the *direct* effect), it can (Section 1.2).
2. Scored against the marginal effect, the best rule found (`embed_prior`)
   ties `donor_wls` to the fourth digit, and its output does not change
   when the embedding is scrambled (Sections 3 and 5).
3. Scored against the direct effect, the kept rule `state_adjusted`
   reaches `r fmt(.mean_score("direct", "test", "state_adjusted"))` on the
   held-out split against
   `r fmt(.mean_score("direct", "test", "null_rescaled"))` for the baseline
   and `r fmt(.mean_score("direct", "test", "donor_wls"))` for `donor_wls`,
   and the dev gain carried to test (Section 4).
4. `state_adjusted` depends on the embedding: with the loadings and scores
   scrambled its log fold change moves by
   `r fmt(.scramble("state_adjusted", "donor", "change_in_se_both"), 2)` to
   `r fmt(.scramble("state_adjusted", "donor_arm", "change_in_se_both"), 2)`
   standard errors where donors have states (Section 5).
5. `state_adjusted` is wrong for the marginal effect wherever the arms
   differ in cell state, by construction, so the choice of target is the
   decision that precedes any choice of rule (Section 7).

*How to read.* A green box closes each results section with what that
section changes. The blue box describes the simulated bank once, and a grey
box opens each section that reuses it. The orange box in Section 7 is the
procedure. A reader of the boxes alone gets the argument.

| Stage | What it does | Section |
|---|---|---|
| Definitions | the generator, the two targets, the rules by name, the kept rule in mathematics, the score and the gates | 1 |
| The bank | what was built and what an oracle could reach | 2 |
| Run A | truth: marginal effect | 3 |
| Run B | truth: direct effect | 4 |
| The embedding check | each kept rule with the embedding scrambled | 5 |
| Constants | each numeric constant of `state_adjusted` with its reason | 6 |
| Recommendation | the procedure, and what is left to decide | 7 |

# Definitions

## Notation and the generator

A cohort has cells $c$, genes $g = 1, \dots, p$ and donors
$d = 1, \dots, n$ in two arms $a \in \{0, 1\}$ of $n_0$ controls and $n_1$
cases. The bank's counts follow

$$\log \mu_{cg} = \alpha_g + x_c^\top y_g + a\,\beta_g + \delta_{dg} + (\text{sex and age terms}),
\qquad x_c = u_d + a\,s + e_c,$$

with $A_{cg} \sim \text{Poisson}(\ell_c \lambda_{cg})$ and
$\lambda_{cg} \sim \text{Gamma}(\text{mean } \mu_{cg}, \text{rate } \gamma_g)$.
The state $x_c$ of a cell is its donor's state $u_d$, plus a shift $s$
shared by every case cell, plus the cell's own $e_c$. The loadings $y_g$
say how each gene responds to cell state. $\delta_{dg}$ is the part of the
donor's effect that is idiosyncratic to the gene. Every donor term is
centred so that its exponential has mean 1 within an arm.

eSVD-DE fits $\widehat x_c$ (the scores, cells by $k$), $\widehat y_g$ (the
loadings, genes by $k$) and a coefficient $\widehat z_{gk}$ per gene and
covariate. Its reparameterization makes the scores orthogonal to every
covariate, the arm included. $\ell_{cg}$ below is the fitted library: the
exponential of the fitted covariate terms other than the arm's.

## Two targets

**The marginal effect**
$\beta^{\text{marg}}_g = (\beta_g + s^\top y_g) / \ln 2$ is the log2 ratio
of mean expression between the populations of case and control donors, at
equal depth and covariates. A difference in cell state between the arms
is part of it.

**The direct effect** $\beta^{\text{dir}}_g = \beta_g / \ln 2$ is the
effect at fixed cell state. A difference in cell state between the arms is
excluded from it.

The two coincide unless the arms differ in cell state ($s \ne 0$). They
differ in what the donors' states do to an estimate. A cohort's arms differ
in mean donor state by $s + (\bar u_1 - \bar u_0)$, the population shift
plus the luck of which donors were sampled, and this moves the arm contrast
of gene $g$ by $y_g^\top \{s + (\bar u_1 - \bar u_0)\}$.

- For the direct effect all of that term is error. It lies along the
  loadings, so it can be estimated from the pattern of the arm contrast
  across genes and removed. This is where the embedding lowers the error
  of the log fold change.
- For the marginal effect $y_g^\top s$ is signal and
  $y_g^\top (\bar u_1 - \bar u_0)$ is sampling error, and one cohort
  cannot tell them apart. An unbiased rule must keep the whole term and
  carry its sampling error in the SE. The embedding can then inform the SE
  and nothing else.

eSVD-DE's own convention is the marginal one: the reparameterization moves
the arm's share of the embedding into the case-control coefficient. The
memo fixed the marginal effect as the truth for that reason (its decision
1, made by Claude). Because the embedding cannot help the log fold change
under that truth, the scorer was given a switch and a second run was
scored against the direct effect.

## The rules by name

| Name in the tables | Rule | Uses the embedding | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `null_rescaled` | the pair that 1.2.0 stores (from donor averages of the posterior), shifted and rescaled by its empirical null | through the posterior | baseline of both runs |
| `donor_wls` | the first loop's kept rule: donor-level weighted regression of log pseudobulk ratios, moderated variance | no | reference, stored with the truth; not a candidate |
| `deseq2` | DESeq2 on donor pseudobulk counts | no | reference, stored with the truth |
| `embed_prior` | `donor_wls` with the residual variance moderated toward a trend that also uses the donor variance the embedding predicts for the gene | in the SE's prior only | kept by run A |
| `state_adjusted` | Section 1.4 | in the log fold change and the SE | kept by run B |

## The kept rule of run B: `state_adjusted`

1. *Donor summary.* With $y_{dg}$ the donor's summed counts and
   $L_{dg} = \sum_{c \in d} \ell_{cg}$,
   $l_{dg} = \log\{(y_{dg} + 1/2) / L_{dg}\}$.
2. *Design.* $D$ is the $n \times q$ donor-level matrix of the intercept,
   the arm, and every covariate constant within donors.
3. *Embedding offset.* The donor's embedding offset is
   $$e_{dg} = \log\frac{\sum_{c \in d} \ell_{cg} \exp(\widehat x_c^\top \widehat y_g)}{L_{dg}},$$
   $e^{r}_{dg}$ is its least-squares residual on $D$, and
   $b = \sum_{d,g} e^{r}_{dg}\, l^{r}_{dg} / \sum_{d,g} (e^{r}_{dg})^2$,
   with $l^{r}$ the residual of $l$ on $D$, is one coefficient per cohort.
4. *Donor-level regression.* $l_{dg} - b\, e^{r}_{dg}$ is regressed on $D$
   as in `donor_wls` (donor offsets, precision weights from
   $\tau^2 + \phi / \mu_{dg}$, weighted least squares). This gives the arm
   coefficient $\widehat\theta_g$, its variance factor $a_g$, and the
   residual variance $S_g$ on $\nu = n - q$ degrees of freedom, moderated
   across genes to $\widetilde S_g$. Because $e^{r}$ is orthogonal to the
   arm, $\widehat\theta_g$ is the arm contrast of $l$ itself; subtracting
   $b\, e^{r}$ only takes the donor-to-donor variation along the embedding
   out of $S_g$. Write $v_g = a_g \widetilde S_g$.
5. *Loadings regression.* With
   $m_g = (1,\; \widehat y_g,\; \{\widehat y_{gj} \widehat y_{gj'}\}_{j \le j'})$,
   $\widehat\theta_g$ is regressed on $m_g$ over the genes with weights
   $1 / v_g$, in two passes, the second without the genes whose residual
   exceeded $3 \sqrt{v_g}$ in the first. The fitted coefficients are an
   intercept $c_0$, a vector $\widehat d$ on the loadings and a symmetric
   matrix $\widehat Q$ on their products.
6. *The pair before calibration.*
   $$\widehat\beta^{\,0}_g = \frac{\widehat\theta_g - \widehat y_g^\top \widehat d - \widehat y_g^\top \widehat Q\, \widehat y_g}{\ln 2},
   \qquad s^{0}_g = \frac{\sqrt{v_g + h_g}}{\ln 2},$$
   with $h_g$ the leverage of gene $g$'s loading terms in that regression.
7. *Calibration.* With $(\delta_0, \sigma_0)$ the mean and SD of the
   empirical null fitted by `eSVD2::multtest()` to
   $\widehat\beta^{\,0}_g / s^{0}_g$ and
   $f = \min\{\max(\sigma_0, 1),\; \sqrt{\nu / \max(\nu - k, 1)}\}$, the
   rule reports
   $$\widehat\beta_g = \widehat\beta^{\,0}_g - \delta_0 \cdot \text{median}_g\, s^{0}_g, \qquad s_g = f\, s^{0}_g .$$

**Where the embedding enters, and why.**

- *Step 5, the linear term (the log fold change).* The arms' difference in
  mean donor state moves $\widehat\theta_g$ by $y_g^\top d$. The fit holds
  the scores orthogonal to the arm, so that term is not in the scores; it
  is in the arm contrast, along the loadings, and $\widehat d$ is five
  numbers estimated from 600 genes.
- *Step 5, the quadratic term (the log fold change).*
  $\widehat\theta_g$ is a contrast of mean log expression, which differs
  from the log ratio of mean expression by half the difference of the
  arms' donor variances on the log scale. The part of that difference that
  comes from donor states is $y_g^\top (\Sigma_1 - \Sigma_0)\, y_g / 2$, a
  quadratic form in the loadings, and $\widehat Q$ estimates it.
- *Step 3 (the SE).* The states' donor-to-donor variation no longer moves
  $\widehat\beta^{\,0}_g$ once step 5 has removed its arm contrast, so it
  must leave the variance too, and $b\, e^{r}$ takes it out of $S_g$.
- *Step 7 (the SE).* The offset was fitted to the same counts and absorbs
  part of the idiosyncratic donor noise within arms, while the arm contrast
  of that noise went to the case-control coefficient and stays in
  $\widehat\theta_g$. $S_g$ therefore understates, by a factor that the
  empirical null measures and that the offset's $k$ free directions among
  $\nu$ bound.

```{r rule_code, echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE, code=readLines("RULE_nov11_direct_claude.R")}
```

## The score and the gates

The score of a cohort is the Gaussian negative log-likelihood of the truth
under the reported pair, in nats per gene, and lower is better,

$$\text{NLL} = \frac{1}{p}\sum_{g=1}^{p}\left[\tfrac12 \log\!\left(2\pi s_g^2\right) + \frac{(\widehat\beta_g - \beta_g)^2}{2 s_g^2}\right].$$

The truth $\beta_g$ is the marginal effect in run A and the direct effect
in run B (`ESVD2_TRUTH`), and every block prints the score against both.
A commit is kept when its paired gain over the best commit is positive and
at least one paired standard error over the `r num_dev` dev examples, and
when it passes two gates. `slope_weak`, the slope of the reported log fold
change on the truth over weak-effect genes, must lie in $[0.9, 1.1]$, so
that shrinkage toward zero fails. `se_strong` is new: the SE of
strong-effect genes over the SE that genes of the same expression level
without a strong effect have, pooled over the examples, must lie in
$[0.92, 1.08]$, so that an SE which follows the estimate fails. The rule
that the first run withdrew by hand gives `se_strong` 1.20 on this bank,
and the valid reference rules 0.97 to 1.04.

# The bank

::: {.generator}
The bank `lfcse-bank-2` holds `r num_dev` dev and `r num_test` test
examples. An example is one cohort of 600 genes generated from the model
of Section 1.1 and fitted end to end by eSVD2 1.2.0 at rank 5. Nine
factors vary. Six are the first bank's: donors (10, 20, 40), cells per
donor (50 equal; unequal, 30 to 600), effects (`sparse`, `sparse_up`,
`dense`), covariates (none; donor sex and age), donor SD (0.2, 0.5, now
varying between genes), and `expression` in place of the rate range
(`high`: the first bank's gene intercepts; `low`: sparse genes, for which
the cap on the nuisance rate binds). Three are new. `state`: `none`
($u_d = 0$, $s = 0$, the first bank's case), `donor` (donor states carry
about 72% of the donor variance), `donor_arm` (the same, with an arm shift
$s$). `arm_sd`: the cases' donor variance is 1.5 times and the controls'
0.5 times the common value. `depth`: each donor shifts a block of 15% of
the genes, which moves its total count and so every other gene's adjusted
level. Each split is a balanced 1/6 fraction of the 1728 combinations, and
the two splits share no combination. `BANK.md` records the bank as built.
:::

```{r bank_table}
bank_table_df <- data.frame(
  quantity = c("Genes capped or at the boundary, `expression = high`",
               "Genes capped or at the boundary, `expression = low`",
               "Mean count per cell and gene, `high` and `low`",
               "Cells per cohort, 10 and 40 donors"),
  realized = c(
    paste0(fmt(100 * .check("expression", "high", "frac_cap_or_boundary"), 0),
           "%"),
    paste0(fmt(100 * .check("expression", "low", "frac_cap_or_boundary"), 0),
           "% (first bank: 13%; real cohorts: 73%)"),
    paste0(fmt(.check("expression", "high", "mean_count"), 2), " and ",
           fmt(.check("expression", "low", "mean_count"), 2)),
    paste0(fmt(.check("donors", "10", "num_cells"), 0), " and ",
           fmt(.check("donors", "40", "num_cells"), 0), " on average")
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(bank_table_df, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Quantity", "Realized"),
             caption = "Table 1. Realized values of the bank, both splits.")
```

**What an ideal use of the embedding could reach.** `oracle_state` is
`donor_wls` with each donor's true state effect subtracted beforehand, and
`oracle_all` subtracts the donor's whole true effect and leaves sampling
noise.

```{r oracle_table}
oracle_table_df <- data.frame(
  state = c("none", "donor", "donor_arm"),
  wls = vapply(c("none", "donor", "donor_arm"), .oracle, numeric(1),
               column = "wls"),
  oracle_state = vapply(c("none", "donor", "donor_arm"), .oracle, numeric(1),
                        column = "oracle_state"),
  oracle_all = vapply(c("none", "donor", "donor_arm"), .oracle, numeric(1),
                      column = "oracle_all"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(oracle_table_df, row.names = FALSE, digits = 3,
             col.names = c("`state`", "`donor_wls`", "`oracle_state`",
                           "`oracle_all`"),
             caption = "Table 2. Dev scores of `donor_wls` and of two oracles that read the truth, against the marginal effect.")
```

The donor states hold about
`r fmt(.oracle("donor", "wls") - .oracle("donor", "oracle_state"), 2)`
nats per gene at the two levels that have them. The oracle knows which
part of the arms' state difference is the population shift $s$; no rule
does, which is the point of Section 1.2.

# Run A: the marginal effect

::: {.reuse}
The bank of Section 2, scored against the marginal effect.
:::

| | |
|---|---|
| Branch | `autoresearch_lfcse2/nov11`, from `r .code(.results("marginal")$commit[1])` |
| Budget agreed | 40 experiments or 4 hours, 8 cores |
| Experiments | `r nrow(.results("marginal")) - 1`: `r .num_status("marginal", "keep")` kept, `r .num_status("marginal", "discard")` discarded |
| What stopped it | a decision, after the experiments had shown what Section 1.2 argues: every rule that changed the log fold change through the embedding lost, and the kept rule equals `donor_wls` |
| Best commit | `r .code(.best_commit("marginal"))` (`embed_prior`) |

```{r run_a_table}
knitr::kable(.experiment_table("marginal"), row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("#", "Commit", "Status", "Dev score",
                           "Change against the best at the time",
                           "Description as logged"),
             caption = "Table 3. Every experiment of run A. Directions E1 to E6 are the memo's. Scores are against the marginal effect; negative changes are gains.")
```

```{r fig_a_trajectory, out.width="80%", fig.align="center", fig.cap="Figure 1. Run A: the dev score of every experiment, kept commits filled."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figure_dir, "marginal_trajectory.png"))
```

Four experiments used the embedding to change the donor summaries or the
design (2, 3, 4 and 8). Each left the log fold change where it was, because
the fitted scores are orthogonal to the arm, and each made the SE too
small, because the donor variation it removed from the residuals still
moves the arm contrast. Experiment 5 added that variation back and reached
`r fmt(.results("marginal")$score[6], 4)`, and experiment 6 moved it into
the prior of the moderation and reached
`r fmt(.results("marginal")$score[7], 4)`.

```{r run_a_result}
.result_table <- function(run){
  rule_vec <- c("null_rescaled", "donor_wls", best_rule_vec[[run]])
  data.frame(
    rule = .code(rule_vec),
    dev = vapply(rule_vec, function(rule){fmt(.mean_score(run, "dev", rule), 4)},
                 character(1)),
    test = vapply(rule_vec, function(rule){
      fmt(.mean_score(run, "test", rule), 4)
    }, character(1)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}
knitr::kable(.result_table("marginal"), row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Rule", "Dev", "Test"), align = "lrr",
             caption = "Table 4. Run A: scores against the marginal effect.")
```

`embed_prior` gains
`r fmt(-.paired("marginal", "test", "null_rescaled")$difference)` nats on
the baseline on test
(`r fmt(-.paired("marginal", "test", "null_rescaled")$difference / .paired("marginal", "test", "null_rescaled")$se, 0)`
paired SE), all of it from leaving the posterior for a donor-level
regression. Against `donor_wls` its difference on test is
`r fmt(.paired("marginal", "test", "donor_wls")$difference, 4)`
(paired SE `r fmt(.paired("marginal", "test", "donor_wls")$se, 4)`).

::: {.takeaway}
Against the marginal effect, no rule that uses the embedding beat
`donor_wls`. The best one is `donor_wls` with a second covariate in its
variance prior, and it scores the same to the fourth digit. This is what
Section 1.2 predicts and not a failure of the search: the scores are
orthogonal to the arm, so they cannot move the arm contrast, and the part
of the contrast that lies along the loadings cannot be removed without
removing a real difference between the arms.
:::

# Run B: the direct effect

::: {.reuse}
The bank of Section 2, scored against the direct effect
(`ESVD2_TRUTH=direct`). The two truths differ only at `state = donor_arm`.
:::

| | |
|---|---|
| Branch | `autoresearch_lfcse2/nov11-direct`, from `r .code(.results("direct")$commit[1])` |
| Budget agreed | 40 experiments or 4 hours, 8 cores |
| Experiments | `r nrow(.results("direct")) - 1`: `r .num_status("direct", "keep")` kept, `r .num_status("direct", "discard")` discarded |
| What stopped it | a decision: the kept rule was at the oracle row of Table 2 where donors have states (`r fmt(.stratum("direct", "dev", "state_adjusted", "state", "donor"))` at `donor` and `r fmt(.stratum("direct", "dev", "state_adjusted", "state", "donor_arm"))` at `donor_arm` on dev, against the oracle's `r fmt(.oracle("donor", "oracle_state"))` and `r fmt(.oracle("donor_arm", "oracle_state"))`), and the last two experiments were a tie and an ablation |
| Best commit | `r .code(.best_commit("direct"))` (`state_adjusted`) |

```{r run_b_table}
knitr::kable(.experiment_table("direct"), row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("#", "Commit", "Status", "Dev score",
                           "Change against the best at the time",
                           "Description as logged"),
             caption = "Table 5. Every experiment of run B. Scores are against the direct effect; negative changes are gains.")
```

```{r fig_b_trajectory, out.width="80%", fig.align="center", fig.cap="Figure 2. Run B: the dev score of every experiment, kept commits filled."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figure_dir, "direct_trajectory.png"))
```

Five commits were kept. The first removed the loadings component of the
arm contrast and took the residual variance free of the embedding offset
(`r fmt(-.results("direct")$delta[2])` nats). The second rescaled the SE
by the empirical null's SD (`r fmt(-.results("direct")$delta[4])`), the
third weighted the loadings regression and made it robust
(`r fmt(-.results("direct")$delta[5])`), the fourth bounded the rescaling
(`r fmt(-.results("direct")$delta[8])`), and the fifth added the products
of the loadings (`r fmt(-.results("direct")$delta[9])`), which removed the
whole penalty of unequal donor variance between the arms.

```{r run_b_result}
knitr::kable(.result_table("direct"), row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Rule", "Dev", "Test"), align = "lrr",
             caption = "Table 6. Run B: scores against the direct effect.")
```

```{r run_b_paired}
paired_table_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("dev", "test"), function(split){
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c("null_rescaled", "donor_wls"), function(reference){
    res <- .paired("direct", split, reference)
    data.frame(split = split, reference = .code(reference),
               difference = fmt(res$difference, 4), se = fmt(res$se, 4),
               ratio = fmt(-res$difference / res$se, 0),
               improved = paste0(res$num_improved, " of ", res$num_examples),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
}))
knitr::kable(paired_table_df, row.names = FALSE, align = "llrrrr",
             col.names = c("Split", "Against", "`state_adjusted` minus it",
                           "Paired SE", "Gain in paired SE",
                           "Examples improved"),
             caption = "Table 7. Run B: paired comparisons over the examples of each split.")
```

The dev gain over the baseline,
`r fmt(-.paired("direct", "dev", "null_rescaled")$difference)` nats,
carried to the test split
(`r fmt(-.paired("direct", "test", "null_rescaled")$difference)`), whose
combinations of factor levels the run never scored. On test the RMSE of
the log fold change is
`r fmt(.block("rmse", "direct", "test", "state_adjusted"))` against
`r fmt(.block("rmse", "direct", "test", "null_rescaled"))` for the
baseline, the coverage of $\widehat\beta_g \pm 1.96\, s_g$ is
`r fmt(.block("coverage_95", "direct", "test", "state_adjusted"))`, and
the SD of $\widehat\beta_g / s_g$ over exactly null genes is
`r fmt(.block("z_sd_null", "direct", "test", "state_adjusted"), 2)`. Both
gates pass (`slope_weak`
`r fmt(.block("slope_weak", "direct", "test", "state_adjusted"))`,
`se_strong`
`r fmt(.block("se_strong", "direct", "test", "state_adjusted"))`).

```{r fig_b_strata, out.width="95%", fig.align="center", fig.cap="Figure 3. Run B: mean score per stratum with one standard error, for the baseline, `donor_wls` and `state_adjusted`, on dev and on test."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figure_dir, "direct_strata.png"))
```

`state_adjusted` is below both other rules in every stratum of both
splits. On test it scores
`r fmt(.stratum("direct", "test", "state_adjusted", "state", "donor"))` at
`state = donor` and
`r fmt(.stratum("direct", "test", "state_adjusted", "state", "donor_arm"))`
at `donor_arm`, where `donor_wls` scores
`r fmt(.stratum("direct", "test", "donor_wls", "state", "donor"))` and
`r fmt(.stratum("direct", "test", "donor_wls", "state", "donor_arm"))`. At
`state = none`, where the embedding has no donor structure to find, it
scores
`r fmt(.stratum("direct", "test", "state_adjusted", "state", "none"))`
against `r fmt(.stratum("direct", "test", "donor_wls", "state", "none"))`,
so the adjustment costs nothing when there is nothing to adjust.

```{r fig_b_paired, out.width="80%", fig.align="center", fig.cap="Figure 4. Run B: the difference `state_adjusted` minus the baseline for each test example, sorted, colored by `state`."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figure_dir, "direct_paired.png"))
```

```{r fig_b_chosen, out.width="85%", fig.align="center", fig.cap="Figure 5. Run B: the median standard error reported per test example, `state_adjusted` against the baseline, by `state` and donor SD; the grey line marks equality."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(figure_dir, "direct_chosen.png"))
```

The median SE of `state_adjusted` is below the baseline's where donors
have states, most at donor SD 0.5, which is the donor-to-donor variation
that the adjustment took out of both the estimate and its variance.

::: {.takeaway}
For the effect at fixed cell state, the embedding is worth
`r fmt(-.paired("direct", "test", "donor_wls")$difference, 2)` nats per
gene over `donor_wls` on held-out cohorts
(`r .paired("direct", "test", "donor_wls")$num_improved` of
`r .paired("direct", "test", "donor_wls")$num_examples` improved) and
`r fmt(-.paired("direct", "test", "null_rescaled")$difference, 2)` over
the posterior-based baseline, with a calibrated Wald statistic. The gain
comes from the loadings, through a regression of the arm contrast on them
across genes, and from the scores, through the residual variance.
:::

# Does each kept rule use the embedding?

::: {.reuse}
Every fourth dev example of the bank (`r length(unique(scramble_df$id))`
cohorts). Each rule file is sourced alone and run on the cohort's view, on
the view with the rows of the scores permuted across cells, and on the
view with the rows of the loadings permuted across genes as well
(`diagnostics/scramble_check_claude.R`).
:::

```{r scramble_table}
scramble_table_df <- scramble_mean_df[order(scramble_mean_df$rule,
                                            scramble_mean_df$state),
                                      c("rule", "state", "change_in_se",
                                        "change_in_se_both", "se_ratio",
                                        "score_direct",
                                        "score_direct_scrambled",
                                        "score_direct_both")]
scramble_table_df$rule <- .code(scramble_table_df$rule)
knitr::kable(scramble_table_df, row.names = FALSE, digits = 3,
             col.names = c("Rule", "`state`",
                           "Median change of the logFC in SE, scores scrambled",
                           "The same, scores and loadings scrambled",
                           "SE ratio, scores scrambled",
                           "Score (direct)", "Score, scores scrambled",
                           "Score, both scrambled"),
             caption = "Table 8. Each kept rule with the embedding scrambled, by `state`.")
```

`embed_prior` moves by about
`r fmt(.scramble("embed_prior", "donor", "change_in_se"), 2)` standard
errors and scores the same when the embedding is scrambled. By the memo's
own standard (a rule whose embedding term could be deleted without
changing the method), it does not use the embedding. `state_adjusted`
uses both parts: scrambling the scores widens its SE by a factor of
`r fmt(.scramble("state_adjusted", "donor", "se_ratio"), 2)` to
`r fmt(.scramble("state_adjusted", "donor_arm", "se_ratio"), 2)` where
donors have states, and scrambling the loadings as well moves its log fold
change by
`r fmt(.scramble("state_adjusted", "donor", "change_in_se_both"), 2)` to
`r fmt(.scramble("state_adjusted", "donor_arm", "change_in_se_both"), 2)`
standard errors and takes its score from
`r fmt(.scramble("state_adjusted", "donor_arm", "score_direct"))` to
`r fmt(.scramble("state_adjusted", "donor_arm", "score_direct_both"))` at
`donor_arm`.

**The price.** On these cohorts `state_adjusted` scores
`r fmt(.scramble("state_adjusted", "donor_arm", "score_marginal"), 2)`
against the marginal effect at `donor_arm`, against
`r fmt(.scramble("embed_prior", "donor_arm", "score_marginal"), 2)` for
`embed_prior`. It removes the arms' difference in cell state and reports a
small SE, so it is confidently wrong as an estimate of the marginal effect
whenever that difference is real. On the whole test split its score
against the marginal effect is
`r fmt(.block("score_marginal", "direct", "test", "state_adjusted"))`.

::: {.takeaway}
Run A's rule satisfies the constraint in letter only, and run B's rule
satisfies it in substance. `state_adjusted` and the marginal effect are
incompatible by construction: the rule is right for the effect at fixed
cell state and wrong for the log ratio of mean expression whenever the
arms differ in cell state.
:::

# Constants

The truth was not on trial within either run. `state_adjusted` has these
numeric constants, and the dev split chose the value of none of them.

| Constant | Where | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| 1/2 | half count in $l_{dg}$ (step 1) | continuity correction of a Poisson count, which keeps the logarithm finite at a zero count |
| 0 | floor of $\tau^2$ and $\phi$ (step 4) | a variance component is not negative |
| 50, $10^{-8}$ | trigamma inverse in the moderation (step 4) | iteration cap and single-precision tolerance of Newton's method |
| 3 | exclusion threshold of the loadings regression, in SE (step 5) | a normal residual is beyond 3 SE once in 370 genes, so a gene beyond it is taken to carry an effect of its own |
| 2 | passes of the loadings regression (step 5) | one pass to find those genes, one without them; a third pass changed the score by `r fmt(.results("direct")$delta[10], 4)` |
| 1 | lower bound of the SE factor (step 7) | removing the offset cannot make the residual variance too large |
| $\sqrt{\nu / (\nu - k)}$ | upper bound of the SE factor (step 7) | the offset has $k$ free directions among the $\nu$ residual ones and cannot have absorbed more than that share |

# Recommendation

Three statements follow from the evidence of this bank. The embedding
improves the log fold change only for the effect at fixed cell state
(Sections 1.2, 3 and 4). For that target `state_adjusted` is the best rule
found, its gain holds on held-out cohorts, and its Wald statistic is
calibrated (Section 4). For the marginal effect `donor_wls` remains the
best rule known, and no use of the embedding improved it (Section 3).

The decisions below are choices the evidence does not settle, and they are
Kevin's.

1. **The target.** Whether eSVD-DE's reported log fold change is the
   marginal effect (the package's current convention, and what the
   p-value tests) or the effect at fixed cell state. The second treats a
   difference in cell state between cases and controls as a nuisance,
   which is also a scientific claim about the disease.
2. **The memo's decisions.** Its section 6 lists nine choices Claude made
   without a round: the truth, the form of the `state` factor, rank 5,
   single cohorts, the `expression` factor, the second gate and its
   interval, the baseline, how the embedding constraint is checked, and
   the split of the design.
3. **The second run.** Scoring against the direct effect was added during
   the session, after run A's first experiments, and was not in the memo.
4. **Merging.** Both run branches and the loop folder are local commits;
   nothing is merged or pushed.

::: {.recipe}
For one cohort fitted by `eSVD()` with the fit kept, when the target is
the effect at fixed cell state:

1. **Inputs.** The counts, the fitted library `library_mat`, the design
   matrix, the donor and arm of each cell, and the embedding `x_mat`,
   `y_mat`.
2. **Check.** Each arm has at least 5 donors, and $n - q \ge 2$. The bank
   does not cover fewer.
3. **Fit.** `report_lfc_se(view)` of `RULE_nov11_direct_claude.R`, which
   is `state_adjusted` (Section 1.4, steps 1 to 7).
4. **Output.** `log2fc` and `se` per gene; the Wald statistic is
   `log2fc / se`, referred to the standard normal distribution.
5. **Report alongside.** The removed vector $\widehat d$ and the share of
   the variance of $\widehat\theta_g$ over genes that the loadings
   regression explains, the SE factor $f$ and whether it sits at a bound,
   and the log fold change of `donor_wls` beside it.
6. **When the target is the marginal effect instead.** Use `donor_wls`
   (`autoresearch_lfcse/notes/RULE_nov11_claude.R`). A large explained
   share in step 5 then says how much of the reported contrast is a
   difference in cell state, with the caveat that part of it is donor
   sampling.
:::

**Three next experiments.**

1. *The rank (a bank factor).* Every cohort was fitted at rank 5 against 3
   or 4 true directions. Real fits use ranks near or above the number of
   donors, where the scores can absorb all donor-level variation and the
   bound of step 7 no longer binds. A `rank` factor (5, 15, 30) tests
   whether `state_adjusted` survives.
2. *Effects aligned with the loadings (a bank factor).* The direct
   effects are drawn independently of the loadings. If the disease acts
   through a gene program that the embedding has also learned, the
   loadings regression removes part of the true effect; `slope_weak` fell
   from `r fmt(.block("slope_weak", "direct", "dev", "null_rescaled"))` to
   `r fmt(.block("slope_weak", "direct", "dev", "state_adjusted"))`
   already with independent effects, because 20 regressors over 600 genes
   take that share of any effect.
3. *The SE factor at 40 donors (direction E4).* Without the rescaling the
   score at 40 donors is better
   (experiment `r max(.results("direct")$experiment)` of run B), and the
   empirical null's SD is inflated there by true weak effects. A
   calibration that does not read the genes' own statistics would recover
   it.

# What we glossed over

- **Real cohorts.** No real cohort was read. Whether the loadings of a
  real fit carry the arm contrast as they do here is untested, and it is
  the first check before the rule is used.
- **One cohort per example.** The two moments of Was2CoDE's Figure 4 need
  pairs of cohorts and were dropped from this bank.
- **The capped share** is `r fmt(100 * .check("expression", "low", "frac_cap_or_boundary"), 0)`%
  at `expression = low`, still below the real cohorts' 73%. Neither kept
  rule reads the nuisance rate.
- **An experiment with a units error.** Experiment 4 of run A added an
  unweighted variance to a weighted one; it was logged as a discard and
  corrected in experiment 5, which was kept.
- **A scorer change after the first baseline.** The switch between the two
  truths and the two extra score lines were added after the bank's
  baseline and before any experiment; the baseline was scored again.
- **The trial function's random seed.** The fresh-context review found
  that it coincided with the stream that drew the true effects; it was
  moved in this loop's scorer. The first loop's scorer has the same
  collision and was not changed, and no rule of either loop draws random
  numbers.
- **Budget.** The runs used `r nrow(.results("marginal")) - 1` and
  `r nrow(.results("direct")) - 1` of 40 experiments each and were stopped
  by decision, for the reasons in Sections 3 and 4.
- **The package's p-value** was again not on trial.

# Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `notes/RULE_nov11_direct_claude.R` | `state_adjusted`, self-contained; mirrors the best commit of run B |
| `notes/RULE_nov11_marginal_claude.R` | `embed_prior`, self-contained; mirrors the best commit of run A |
| `notes/RUN_nov11_claude.md` | the run report in the protocol's format |
| `notes/MEMO_claude.md`, `notes/BANK.md` | the design with its decisions to confirm, and the bank as built |
| `diagnostics/report_run_nov11_claude.R` | writes `notes/csv/RUN_nov11/` and `notes/figures/RUN_nov11/` from the untracked `output/` |
| `diagnostics/scramble_check_claude.R` | writes `csv/RUN_nov11/scramble.csv` |
| `diagnostics/bank_checks_claude.R` | realized values of the bank and the oracle rows |
| `csv/RUN_nov11/results.csv` | one row per logged commit of each run, the baseline first |
| `csv/RUN_nov11/scores.csv` | one row per example, run, split and rule |
| `csv/RUN_nov11/blocks.csv` | one row per line of a summary block |
| `csv/RUN_nov11/scramble.csv`, `oracle_dev.csv`, `bank_checks.csv` | Table 8, Table 2 and Table 1 |

**Reproducibility.** The bank is `lfcse-bank-2`, with `r num_dev` dev and
`r num_test` test rows in its manifests; the scorer's budget is 600
seconds on 8 cores. The best commit of run B is rescored by
`git checkout `r .best_commit("direct")` && ESVD2_TRUTH=direct Rscript autoresearch_lfcse2/harness/evaluate_claude.R dev`,
and that of run A by the same command at
`r .code(.best_commit("marginal"))` without the variable. The diagnostics
scripts are run from the repository root with `Rscript`.
